$comment: Retired vocabulary: names this project STOPPED using, and must not start using again.
THIS IS A DENYLIST, AND HERE THAT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE. The publication guard is an
allowlist because naming a private thing in a guard publishes it. Everything below is
PUBLIC BY CONSTRUCTION — a removed CRD field, a withdrawn tiebreak, a superseded
command — so listing it costs nothing, and the list IS the value: it is the record of
what this project stopped doing, in the one place that fails a build when it comes back.
Each entry: `pattern` (Python regex, searched case-insensitively unless `case` is true),
`says` (what to write instead — printed on a hit), and `allow` (regexes that mark a line
as RECORDING the removal rather than asserting the thing). The allow list is what lets a
spec say 'spec.type is removed' while failing one that says 'required spec.type'.
A MIGRATION-TABLE ROW IS A RECORD, and several `allow` entries below say so by
matching the REPLACEMENT name rather than a marker word. A line reading
`| persistence.enabled | persistence.context.enabled |` states what to write
instead, which is the whole test — and a wide table cannot carry 'removed' on
every row without becoming unreadable. The window is one line either side, so
a header word does not reach row four.
`skip` names files inside `scan` that are NOT checked. There is exactly one, and it
is the CHANGELOG: its job is to record what each version removed, so it accumulates
every name this guard exists to catch. An entry for a RELEASED version must also not
be edited to satisfy a guard added afterwards — somebody may be following it. The
archives under docs/changelog/ were never scanned for the same reason: `docs/*.md`
does not recurse.

terms.says: a Channel or SignalSource names its serving adapter in spec.adapter; spec.type was removed
a Channel carries no delivery hints; the operator owns delivery
a Channel supplies no profile; the Pipelines claiming the chat source decide who answers
sources are shareable; the conflict condition was deleted
there is no creation-order tiebreak anywhere; several claimants are answered with the choices
channels originate nothing; there is no pipeline-for-channel lookup
the listing command is /pipelines; /agents still answers and is never printed, offered or registered
there is no HTTP form that names a Pipeline; POST /task was deleted
the handle is runtimeContextId; sessionId is the retired spelling, dual-read for one release
ingest is on when the router runs; Channel.spec.config.pollingEnabled is gone
the cap is MAX_ACTIVE_CONVERSATIONS; MAX_RUNTIMES is the deprecated alias
the bundle is prometheus-bundle and the adapter is alertmanager; both were renamed
the channel-adapter workload and Service are agentops-adapter-<name>
$comment: THE IMAGE IS NOT THE SERVICE, AND THE STRING IS IDENTICAL.
channels/telegram publishes agentops-channel-telegram — the path IS the
published name, per .claude/rules/structure.md — so an image reference
spells the retired Service name exactly. The lookbehind is what tells them
apart: an image is written under its registry path, a Service name is not.
Found when archiving sdlc-setup folded a release spec naming that image
into openspec/specs/, and the guard failed on correct text.

terms.says: delivery is decided per DESTINATION; the origin-kind rule was deleted
it is an agent runtime, not a worker
a signal STARTS a conversation; nothing is asleep. 'Wake' is correct only for a PERSON
delivery is per DESTINATION — every bound channel that has not already displayed it
sources are shareable; any number of Ready Pipelines may claim one
the CONTEXT volume — it is named for what it HOLDS, a conversation's accumulated context, not for the filesystem path one runtime image happens to mount it at

an AgentRuntime declares NO volume at all: persistence is wiring and lives on Pipeline.spec.persistence, with the chart's release-wide claim below it. The field was DELETED rather than aliased, because its concept moved to another CR
the runtime names no claim: set persistence.context / persistence.workspace release-wide, or pipelines[].persistence for one route
CONTEXT_PVC — and it is not dual-read, because the concept moved to another CR
agentops-context — the default claim was renamed with the volume, and the chart FAILS the render rather than silently provisioning a second, empty one
the block moved wholesale: persistence.context.* and persistence.workspace.*
/data/context — the mount path moved with the name. /data/workspace is the load-bearing path and it did NOT move

an account STATES ITS RULES — clusterRoles, bindClusterRoles or namespaced — or holds nothing. There is no preset posture at ANY level: a mode name is a grant nobody reviewed, and declaring the account rather than defaulting it release-wide does not make the word readable
an account a route names is one the install DECLARES under rbac.runtime.serviceAccounts; nothing renders a posture-named account on its own
the runtime block split in two: global.agentops.runtimeDefaults for what every runtime inherits, and the top-level `runtimes:` list for the runtimes that exist
global.agentops.runtimeDefaults.* — the block was renamed when it became a complete runtime configuration
those moved ONTO an account: declare it under rbac.runtime.serviceAccounts and put clusterRoles / bindClusterRoles / namespaced on the entry
global.agentops.runtimeDefaults.idleTtlMinutes — a bundle-shipped runtime cannot read a parent-scope value

every subchart is named for the SYSTEM it integrates, with no suffix — the VALUES KEY and the chart directory are `kubernetes`, `home-assistant`, `telegram`, `prometheus`. (The openspec CAPABILITY names are unchanged, which is why this matches only a key, a path or a values line.)
an adapter names the ServiceAccount it runs as — `spec.serviceAccountName`, a reference the chart creates — and naming one is what mounts its token. Absent means the release floor, denied every verb
every openspec change is implemented in its own worktree on change/<name> and lands as one pull request; committing straight to master was retired with the shared checkout that forced it

the review is the four jobs of .github/workflows/claude-review.yml — a program builds the queue, one `read` job per changed component, `consolidate` runs the coordinator, `reconcile` resolves — dispatched by hand with `gh workflow run claude-review.yml -f number=<pr>`; the in-session dynamic workflow was retired because its reader pool was two on a four-core runner

a component is read per FILE by `file-reviewer` subagents that a saved workflow (`review-component.js`) starts inside the component's read job, each in a context holding that file and the rules routed to its path; the one reader holding a whole component's diff grew with the diff

a component is read PER FILE, each in its own `claude -p` process the `read` job starts from the shell, holding the rules routed to the component's paths as a cached system prefix — there is no queue of files inside one reader's context, and no reader pool to size
the read job is a shell loop over one `claude -p` per file; review-component.js and its saved-workflow indirection were deleted
`.mcp.json` reads the analysis through SonarCloud's own hosted MCP endpoint (`https://api.sonarcloud.io/mcp`), not the Dockerised sonarqube-mcp-server -- see CONTRIBUTING.md, "Code analysis"
conveyor:fix replaces autofix (the approve label), and conveyor:implement replaces autoimplement

a thread resolution is not an Actions trigger; no check reads the review's threads or the loop's disputes, branch protection holds the merge live, and conveyor-sweep.yml resumes a waiting loop once its disputes are resolved

`.github/scripts/carry.py` is the one carry and it asks `conveyor.py`: the two programs it replaced held the grant rule in two copies, and the gate held a third — see .claude/rules/worktree-delivery.md
a person's comment on a waiting pull request starts a round; no check reads a person's answer and nothing is re-run on it
no required check reads the loop's conversation, so no job is re-run on a person's answer; the round reads it
the ops poll names its adapter with ?adapter=<name>. ?type= was replaced
the dispute guard is the archive command's alone (autofix-guard.py, no purpose flag); docs-task never fails on a dispute
the pipeline-run cluster pack lives at platform/manager/test/system/; test/e2e/ was renamed
the pack's build tag is `system`; the `e2e` build tag was renamed
the pack's workflows are system.yml/system-smoke.yml/system-full.yml; e2e.yml/e2e-smoke.yml/e2e-full.yml were renamed
the pack's knobs are SYSTEM_TIER/SYSTEM_ARTIFACT_DIR/SYSTEM_BUDGET/SYSTEM_REUSE/SYSTEM_SKIP_BUILD; the E2E_* names were renamed
apiBase is the router's alone, and channel-telegram reaches the Bot API only through the gateway binding

terms.pattern: (channel[- ]telegram|channel adapter).{0,80}(calls|sends to|posts to|talks to|reaches|reads|uses|holds).{0,40}(api\.telegram\.org|bot[- ]?token|Bot API credential|Bot API directly)
terms.says: channel-telegram holds no Telegram credential and relays every Bot API call through the router's /telegram/call instead
wiringEnabled is the bundle-wide switch now, paired with global.agentops.wiringMode for which CRD shape it renders
a signal carries a sender-minted initiationId; the manager's own fingerprint cooldown was removed along with it, replaced by cooldown keyed on initiationId
SignalSource.spec.grouping (signatureLabels, windowDays) was removed outright, with no successor field — correlation is the sender's initiationId, matched by equality
the agentops.dev/signature-hash label was removed with no successor label; equality routing reads an informer field index on spec.conversationId instead
a conversation's identity is spec.conversationId, the adopted initiationId; the manager-computed grouping signature (and Conversation.spec.signature) was removed
ADAPTER_NAME is the one env name carrying an adapter's identity, on channel and signal adapters alike
ADAPTER_NAME is the one env name carrying an adapter's identity, on channel and signal adapters alike
telegram.enabled is the one gate the whole bundle renders under, and the flat telegramAdapter.enabled value gates nothing
the landing page shows the generated readme-flow picture (readme-flow-{light,dark}.svg, theme-resolved); the .ao-presentation component left the theme
AgentProfile.spec.outputFormat is the field's name, a required enum (blocks/none) with no default
the per-kind spec pages under docs/crds/ replaced the single generated reference page
InputItem.origin ({kind, name}) records where every input came from; the job-only jobName field is gone
